text: Irene Vance's studio was insolvent, and Lucien Ravel had not paid her for two years of restoration work.

irene.cover: My studio is doing perfectly well. Lucien and I have an excellent working relationship.
irene.say: The studio is finished. Lucien has not paid me in two years, and the bank stopped waiting in the spring.

lucien.cover: What I owe my contractors is my own affair.
lucien.say: I owe Irene a good deal of money. Two years of invoices. I had other... priorities.

points.note: Insolvent, and owed two years of fees by the gallery.

text: On Monday night Irene put a replica she had cast into the vault and carried the real Nightingale out in her equipment case.

irene.cover: I returned the Nightingale to the vault on Monday exactly as I received it.
irene.say: I put the copy in the vault on Monday. The real bird went out in my equipment case.

points.note: She made the switch when she returned the bird.

text: On Tuesday morning Irene drove to the Halden freight depot and shipped a crate to Antwerp.

irene.cover: On Tuesday I was in my studio all day. I didn't go anywhere.
irene.say: I went to the Halden depot on Tuesday morning and sent a crate to Antwerp.

points.note: She shipped a crate abroad the morning after the bird was returned.

text: Felix Dorn entered the gallery at 01:12 on Wednesday using his own vault code.

felix.cover: I haven't been inside the Ravel Gallery in weeks.
felix.say: Fine — yes. I came in at about ten past one on Wednesday morning. With my own code.

points.note: He was in the vault in the middle of the night and lied about it.

text: Felix came in secretly to replace a faulty vault motion sensor he had installed, and never opened the display case.

felix.cover: I had some routine checks to do. That's all.
felix.say: One of my motion sensors was faulty — my mistake, my install. If Ravel found out I'd lose the contract. I swapped it at night. I never touched the case; my tablet logs everything. You can have it.

points.note: His night visit has an innocent, checkable explanation.

text: Lucien Ravel spent Wednesday night at the Lantern Club card room, from ten until half past three.

lucien.cover: I was at home all Wednesday night. Alone.
lucien.say: I was at the Lantern Club on Wednesday. Cards. From ten until gone three. Hardly a crime.

points.note: He was at a card club, not the gallery, on Wednesday night.

text: Lucien owes more than a million to the syndicate that runs the Lantern Club.

lucien.say: I owe a little over a million to some very patient gentlemen at the Lantern Club. They are becoming less patient.

text: At about 23:30 on Monday Pavel saw Irene leave by the loading door carrying her heavy equipment case.

pavel.cover: Monday was quiet. Staff came and went as usual.
pavel.say: Half eleven Monday, Ms Vance went out the loading door with that big equipment case of hers. Heavy, she was struggling with it. I held the door.

points.note: Seen leaving with a heavy case minutes after closing the vault.

text: At Irene's request Pavel paused the vault corridor camera from 23:00 to 23:20 on Monday, 'for her photographs'.

pavel.cover: The cameras run all the time. Always have.
pavel.say: Ms Vance asked me to pause the corridor camera for twenty minutes on Monday. Said the infrared spoiled her photographs of the enamel. I didn't think anything of it.

points.note: She asked for the vault camera to be switched off while she was inside.

text: Pavel slept through most of his Wednesday shift in the back office and filled in his rounds afterwards.

pavel.cover: I did my rounds every hour on Wednesday. Every hour.
pavel.say: All right. I was asleep in the back office most of Wednesday night. I ticked the rounds off in the morning.

text: Odile found the vault bird was a replica: its enamel was weeks old and the hairline flaw under the left wing, recorded in her 2024 appraisal, was missing.

odile.say: The enamel was weeks old, not a hundred and sixty years. And the hairline flaw under the left wing — I recorded it myself in 2024 — simply wasn't there. Whoever made that copy was very good, and worked from photographs.

points.note: The fake was the work of a skilled enamel specialist.

text: In the spring Irene asked Odile, over dinner, how insurers detect replicas of enamel work.

odile.cover: Clients ask me all sorts of things.
odile.say: In April, over dinner, Irene asked me how an insurer would tell a good enamel replica from an original. Professional curiosity, I assumed.

points.note: She asked an appraiser how replicas are detected.

text: Lucien holds a master override for the vault that does not appear in the access log.

felix.say: Mr Ravel has a master override. It opens the vault and it doesn't write to the log — he insisted on that.

lucien.cover: Only staff codes open that vault.
lucien.say: I have an override. It is my vault, after all.

points.note: He could open the vault without leaving a trace in the log.

text: The insurer, not Lucien, asked for the cover to be raised after a market revaluation.

odile.say: We raised the cover, not Mr Ravel. The market for automata went through the roof; our underwriters insisted.

lucien.say: The insurers raised the cover themselves. I merely signed.

points.note: The higher insurance cover was the insurer's idea.
